final_delta_review: absence_probes is initialized separately from resource samples; every returned absence proof is appended before its guard.
absence-NNN.json uses len(absence_probes)-1 and exclusive durable creation, so failed preflight with no resource sample cannot be overwritten by postflight.
resource_index_if_sampled links a proof to the prospective resource sample index without reusing it as the proof filename.
complete.json reports absence_probes count; the new negative test checks separate before-prepare and postflight files after port-present failure.
Docstring now states SIGKILL/power-loss/unknown-spawn reconciliation limits without changing recovery admission.
protocol_review_scope: Common nonblocking journal lock around STOPPED snapshot plus durable attempt, and around final absence check plus spawn intent plus Popen.
Source/plan/runtime journal binding and actual owner-produced NO_CHILD_STARTED or child release receipts accepted by controller fake tests.
Recovery requires both owner and any spawned child absent; no-experiment cannot bypass an existing owner directory.
POST monitor owns only its HTTP client worker; terminating/reaping it does not cancel or prove termination of the server-side loader.
Unknown load/bootstrap outcomes preserve durable intent and forbid blind duplicate mutation.

validation.reason: Parent requested review of final delta only and supplied frozen CPU test logs.

known_limits: A SIGKILL/power loss after durable attempt but before an explicit NO_CHILD_STARTED terminal stays unresolved; missing intent alone is not proof. Manual reconciliation is required.
Unknown spawn after durable intent also requires reconciliation; no automatic recovery may fabricate a child/reap receipt.
Physical monitoring is sampled observation, not an OS memory hard cap. HTTP cancellation may leave the service-side loader active.
No real cold restart, model restoration, runtime variant restoration or device numerical qualification was performed by this review.
This is a targeted independent static and CPU-protocol review, not a proof against every OS failure or adversarial file modification.
